findings.title: GET /pulls/:id no longer triggers a GitHub refresh
findings.rationale: The GET handler previously attempted to fetch the latest PR data from GitHub and persist it before returning. Now it serves only what is already stored in the database, with no network call. Callers that depended on the side effect (e.g., to ensure fresh data on every view) will silently get stale data. The PR description documents this as intentional, but the change is a behavioral break for any deployed caller that does not also call the new POST /pulls/:id/refresh endpoint.

findings.title: GET /pulls/:id no longer refreshes data from GitHub
findings.rationale: The old handler attempted a live GitHub fetch and persisted the result before returning; the new handler only reads from the database. Any caller that relied on the side effect (e.g., calling GET to both read and refresh) will now silently receive stale data. The response shape is identical, so no caller fails, but the contract's observable behavior changed. The PR description frames this as intentional, but external callers (CI, other services) are not updated in this diff.

findings.title: POST /pulls/:id/refresh does not handle missing GitHub token gracefully
findings.rationale: The old GET handler wrapped the GitHub call in a try-catch and served stored data on failure. The new POST handler calls `container.github()` without a try-catch. If no token is configured, this will throw an unhandled error (likely 500) instead of returning a meaningful error response (e.g., 503 with a message about GitHub not being configured). The client mutation has no onError handler, so the user would see a generic error.

findings.title: useRefreshPull captures prId at creation time instead of using a mutation variable
findings.rationale: The mutationFn closes over `prId` at the time the hook is called. If the component re-renders with a different prId (e.g., navigating between PRs without unmounting), the mutation will still use the stale prId. The component also calls `refreshPull.mutate()` without arguments, so the mutationFn must already have the correct prId. This pattern works when prId is stable but is fragile.

findings.title: useRefreshPull parameter type is narrower than the component's prId type

The existing `usePullDetail` hook accepts `string | number | null | undefined`. This inconsistency could cause a TypeScript error or silent coercion.

matched_title: GET /pulls/:id no longer fetches fresh data from GitHub

findings.title: GET /pulls/:id no longer fetches fresh data from GitHub
findings.rationale: The old handler attempted a live GitHub fetch on every GET and fell back to the DB only on failure. The new handler always serves from the DB without any GitHub call. A deployed caller that relied on GET /pulls/:id to return fresh data (e.g., a CI runner polling for updates) will now silently receive stale data. The PR adds POST /pulls/:id/refresh as the explicit way to get fresh data, but existing callers that do not change their code will break behaviorally.

findings.title: GET /pulls/:id response shape is narrower than before
findings.rationale: The old success path returned `{ ...detail, id: pr.id }` which spread all fields from GitHub's getPullRequest response (e.g., labels, milestone, assignees, requested_reviewers). The new GET handler returns only the fields explicitly listed in the manually constructed object (id, number, title, author, branch, base, head_sha, additions, deletions, files_count, status, opened_at, updated_at, body, files, commits). Any caller that read a field like `labels` from the response will now get `undefined`, potentially causing crashes or incorrect UI. The new POST /pulls/:id/refresh still returns the full GitHub spread, so callers that need those fields must switch to POST first.
